podcast.title: Description in Solo Work
podcast.body: The term "low-fi" was used to describe aspects of Gord Downie's first solo album, "Coke Machine Glow," alongside spoken word elements, indicating a specific recording and musical aesthetic that was difficult to categorize. "Lots of spoken word. Lots of low-fi recording and music that's really really hard to categorize in Pigeon Hole."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Growth Due to Home Recording Gear
podcast.body: The proliferation of cheap and powerful home recording equipment significantly spurred the growth and resurgence of low-fi music. This technology allowed independent artists to create music on limited budgets, fostering a sound that embraced imperfections and a lack of slickness, which became defining characteristics of the genre. "More low-fi, something called Bedroom Pop, a resurgence in sounds like shoegays, new flavors of hip hop."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
